attempts.label: DANDI:000673
attempts.paper_title: Control of working memory by phase–amplitude coupling of human hippocampal neurons
attempts.entry_title: Phase-amplitude coupling and working memory in human hippocampus (Daume et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: The behavioural effects, the weaker hippocampal theta-gamma coupling under higher memory load, and persistent firing of category neurons largely held up, though some of these rest on choices the paper does not state. The reported absences of a load effect outside the hippocampus did not hold, because the pre-SMA differed, probably due to channels removed by the paper's undocumented visual artefact rejection. The findings on coupling neurons (that they are distinct from category neurons and enhance decoding) could not be tested. Only 8 hippocampal neurons qualified against the paper's 79, for a reason the records do not explain. The spike-field coherence analyses were not run.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Daume et al. (2024) on dandiset 000673, which holds 44 sessions of a Sternberg working memory task in 36 epilepsy patients, with 1,454 single neurons and 1,922 microwire LFP channels from the hippocampus, amygdala, pre-SMA, dACC and vmPFC. It tests the cohort, behaviour, category neurons and their maintenance activity, and the LFP theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, its load effect and its controls, single-trial PAC against reaction time and category neuron firing, and the selection and firing of PAC neurons. The spike-field coherence, noise correlation and decoding analyses were not run.

outcomes.notes: 44 sessions of 36 patients (21 female, 15 male, age 40.47 +/- 13.76 years), 1,454 units (hippocampus 360, amygdala 496, pre-SMA 204, dACC 188, vmPFC 206) and 1,922 LFP channels (586, 421, 283, 325, 307), every count equal to the paper's. sub-20 has no LFP. Units of a patient recorded in several sessions are counted once per session, as the paper's total does.

Mean over 44 sessions of the median RT of correct trials, 1.233 s in load 1 and 1.360 s in load 3, both within 10% of 1.33 and 1.46 s; paired permutation t-test t43 = 5.33, p = 0.0001 (paper t43 = 6.42); load 3 slower in 36 of 44 sessions and 29 of 36 patients. With the mean RT per session (variant) load 1 is 1.633 s and load 3 1.596 s (p = 0.66); RTs reach 74.2 s, 69 trials above 10 s.
95.10% in load 1 and 91.02% in load 3 (paper 95.71 and 91.60%); t43 = -5.24, p = 0.0001 (paper t43 = -4.45); load 3 less accurate in 32 of 44 sessions and 27 of 36 patients.

Accuracy 93.05 +/- 7.22% over 44 sessions (range 74.8 to 100%); false negatives 76.08 +/- 20.11% of errors over the 41 sessions with errors (75.29% of all 425 errors pooled). Both within the paper's s.d.

Category neurons 94 of 360 in the hippocampus (26.11%), 181 of 496 in the amygdala (36.49%), 40 of 206 in the vmPFC (19.42%), 18 of 204 in the pre-SMA and 13 of 188 in the dACC, all within 10% of the paper's 89, 181, 37, 18 and 14. Against 500 label shuffles the hippocampus, amygdala and vmPFC exceed the 99th percentile (p = 0.002 each) and the dACC does not (p = 0.088), but the pre-SMA's 18 also exceeds its 99th percentile of 17 (p = 0.010), where the paper reports no excess. With a post hoc threshold of two-sided p < 0.05 the counts are 87, 174, 41, 18 and 14. The pre-SMA sits at the boundary - 18 is one above the 99th percentile and p = 0.010 equals the threshold - so with 500 shuffles neither form of the rule separates it clearly from chance.
deviations: The shuffle permutes the category labels of all presentations of a session together, one shuffle for all its units; the Methods say only that labels were shuffled across presentations. The permutation null of each test is drawn once per unit and reused for the shuffled labellings (the permutation distribution depends only on the values and group sizes).

outcomes.notes: 275 MTL category neurons (paper 270). Maintenance rates exceed baseline in preferred and non-preferred trials under both readings of O6 (p = 0.0001 each). Preferred exceeds non-preferred in % of baseline (32.0 against 20.5%, t = 2.26, p = 0.0013; paper t269 = 2.93, p = 0.001) but not in Hz (2.81 against 2.76 Hz, t = 1.74, p = 0.072). The criterion asks for all three tests under both readings, so the claim holds in part. In 24 of 34 patients the preferred rate is higher. Under reading (b) alone, adopted for fig3c and fig3d, all three tests hold.
deviations: Rates are compared in Hz and in % of each neuron's baseline (O6); the paper does not say which its tests use.

outcomes.notes: In % of baseline the hippocampus (94 neurons) and amygdala (181) pass all three tests (baseline tests p <= 0.0001; preferred against non-preferred p = 0.019 and 0.039; paper 0.025 and 0.037) and the vmPFC (40) passes none (p = 0.064, 0.24, 0.12). In Hz the vmPFC again passes none, but preferred against non-preferred fails in the hippocampus (p = 0.24) and amygdala (p = 0.18). The criterion, through fig3b, asks for both readings, so the claim holds in part.
deviations: As fig3b-persistent-activity (O6 readings).

outcomes.notes: In % of baseline, the reading adopted, preferred trials do not differ between loads (35.29 against 30.85%, t = 0.47, p = 0.77; paper t269 = 2.65, p = 0.004) and non-preferred trials do not either (p = 0.26). In Hz the claim holds (preferred 2.90 against 2.78 Hz, t = 2.20, p = 0.022; non-preferred p = 0.20). The question of the units is for the paper's authors (finding on O6).
deviations: Assumed that the tests use the percentage change from baseline. The readings give different outcomes. The Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 legends say "FRs are shown as the percentage change compared with the baseline" and print the P values with those panels (Fig. 4f gives "correct, P = 0.0001; incorrect, P = 0.0001" against baseline for the plotted values), so the tests are taken to be on the plotted values. The data support this - with at least one incorrect trial, the % of baseline reading gives exactly the paper's n for the frontal areas in Extended Data Fig. 8h (201, 180 and 201; neurons with no baseline spike drop out), and the Hz reading does not (204, 183, 202).

outcomes.notes: In % of baseline over all trials, 251 neurons with at least one incorrect trial (paper 246) fire more in correct than incorrect trials (26.56 against 9.27%, t = 2.50, p = 0.0035; paper t245 = 2.43, p = 0.02); with at least two incorrect trials 229 neurons, p = 0.010; three, 209, p = 0.055. In Hz the test fails under every reading (p >= 0.12), and on preferred trials only it fails in both units (p >= 0.10).
deviations: Assumed the percentage change from baseline (as fig3c-category-load); in Hz the claim is not reproduced. The minimum number of incorrect trials (O7) is not given; 1, 2 and 3 are shown and the first matches the paper's n.

outcomes.notes: Correct preferred trials, median split within load. Hippocampus (94 neurons) fast 2.76 against slow 2.77 Hz, p = 0.85 (in % of baseline p = 0.22); amygdala (181) 2.92 against 2.83 Hz, p = 0.098 (p = 0.51). No test reaches p < 0.05.
deviations: Trials at or below the load's median RT are fast, above it slow (the split of ties is not stated; a standard choice).

outcomes.notes: Panels f and g need spike-field coherence, which was not run in this attempt (fig3f-gamma-sfc-preferred). Panel h was run - with at least one incorrect trial, pre-SMA (204 neurons in Hz, 201 in % of baseline; paper 201) correct 2.91 against incorrect 3.07 Hz, p = 0.039, and in % of baseline p = 0.54; dACC (183 and 180; paper 180) p = 0.83 and 0.71; vmPFC (202 and 201; paper 201) p = 0.60 and 0.97. In % of baseline, the reading adopted for the firing rate tests (fig3c-category-load), panel h holds and its n equal the paper's in all three areas; in Hz the pre-SMA differs with one incorrect trial and not with two or three (p = 0.089, 0.11).

Under artefact reading (a), the mean z-scored MI over 1,922 channels (paper 1,917) is largest (2.16) at phase 4 Hz and amplitude 80 Hz; at phase 4 Hz the amplitude profile has local maxima at 50 Hz (within 30-55) and 80 Hz (within 70-140), and at 6 Hz at 40 and 80 Hz. Under reading (b), computed for phase centres 2 to 8 Hz, the mean over 1,918 channels is largest (1.73) at 4 Hz and 80 Hz, with local maxima at 45 and 80 Hz. Both readings meet the criterion. Per area the maximum is at phase 4 Hz in the hippocampus (75 Hz) and amygdala (50 Hz under a, 45 Hz under b) and at 2 Hz in the frontal areas.
deviations: The visual inspection of the artefact rejection cannot be repeated (O1); both automated readings were run. Under reading (b) the notebook computes phase centres 2 to 8 Hz only, the ones its other claims use.

Filters follow pop_eegfiltnew's default design (windowed sinc, Hamming) and firfilt's edge padding, reimplemented in Python (sbcat.py); the 200 surrogates draw a random permutation of the trials, as cfc_tort_comodulogram.m does.

outcomes.notes: Under artefact reading (a), significant channels are 144 of 586 hippocampal (paper 137), 130 of 421 amygdala (130), 41 of 307 vmPFC (40), 17 of 283 pre-SMA (5) and 14 of 325 dACC (14); all but the pre-SMA are within tolerance. Every area's proportion exceeds the 99th percentile of its surrogate null (O4), p = 0.005 (the smallest possible with 200 surrogates), including the pre-SMA and dACC. Under reading (b) the counts are 125, 112, 27, 12 and 8, with the amygdala, vmPFC, pre-SMA and dACC out of tolerance; the proportions again exceed the null.
deviations: Artefact rejection without the visual inspection (O1), under two readings of the span it is computed on. The counts are judged under reading (a), adopted for the claims where the readings disagree. On the one channel whose rejected trials the paper's code ships (artif_trials.mat with NWB_samplePAC_SU.m, sub-26 session 1, LFP channel 33), the paper removes 17 trials; reading (a) removes 4, all among them, and reading (b) removes 9, 5 of which the paper kept.

outcomes.notes: In the significant hippocampal channels z-scored theta-high-gamma MI is lower in load 3 under both readings - (a) 144 channels, 4.62 against 3.80, t = -4.16, p = 0.0002, FDR p = 0.0010, load 1 higher in 99 channels and in 18 of 23 patients; (b) 125 channels, t = -3.05, FDR p = 0.014. Paper t136 = -4.26, p < 0.001.
deviations: Artefact rejection without the visual inspection (O1); 144 or 125 channels where the paper has 137.

outcomes.notes: With the paper's test and FDR over the five areas, under reading (a) the pre-SMA (17 channels; load 1 1.81, load 3 6.87; FDR p = 0.0017) and the amygdala (130 channels; 3.86 against 4.20, load 3 higher; FDR p = 0.0475) differ between loads; the dACC (FDR p = 0.37) and vmPFC (0.93) do not. Under reading (b) the pre-SMA (12 channels, FDR p = 0.014) and dACC (8 channels, load 1 higher, FDR p = 0.014) differ and the amygdala does not (FDR p = 0.086). The pre-SMA has 17 or 12 significant channels where the paper has 5, and load 1 is higher in only 3 of the 17. The 17 channels come from six patients; four of sub-4 have z values of 19 to 25 in load 3 against 3.5 to 6.8 in load 1, and seven of sub-11 are also higher in load 3. The effect does not rest on a few outliers alone - Wilcoxon p = 0.0011, and without the three channels of largest load 3 excess p = 0.0045 (reading a; under b, p = 0.059).
deviations: Artefact rejection without the visual inspection (O1). The channels that decide the pre-SMA result are channels that the paper's visual inspection may have removed; the files do not say.

outcomes.notes: Under artefact reading (a), 23 patients (paper 23) have hippocampal PAC channels; the patient means are higher in load 1 (3.97 against 3.23, t = 2.26, p = 0.0095; paper p = 0.0049; 18 of 23 patients), and no other area differs (amygdala p = 0.10, pre-SMA 0.31, dACC 0.99, vmPFC 0.92). Under reading (b) the hippocampus gives p = 0.11 over 20 patients and no area differs.
deviations: Assumed artefact reading (a), automated rejection on the -0.5 to 3 s epochs. The two readings give different outcomes. Reading (a) removes 16.0 +/- 12.0 trials per channel (11.4%), below the paper's 20.4 +/- 13.9 (14.6%) that also include the trials removed by visual inspection; reading (b), on whole trials, removes 36.2 +/- 22.8 (25.9%), more than the paper's total. On the one channel whose rejected trials the paper's code ships (artif_trials.mat with NWB_samplePAC_SU.m, sub-26 session 1, LFP channel 33), the paper removes 17 trials; reading (a) removes 4, all among them, and reading (b) removes 9, 5 of which the paper kept.

outcomes.notes: With channels selected on theta-low-gamma PAC (a - 152, 159, 22, 27, 48 channels; paper 148, 155, 10, 22, 48), the pre-SMA differs between loads (load 3 higher, p = 0.0029; FDR variant p = 0.0145); no other area does (p >= 0.11). Under reading (b) the pre-SMA again differs (13 channels, p = 0.0033) and no other area does.
deviations: Artefact rejection without the visual inspection (O1).

outcomes.notes: Under all four combinations of band reading (A phase centres, B direct band filters) and artefact reading, both hippocampal high-gamma tests give p < 0.05 with load 1 higher (fast theta t = -3.44, -3.27, -3.03, -2.50; slow theta t = -2.43, -2.21, -2.46, -2.22), but 8, 5, 6 and 6 of the 20 tests are significant, always including pre-SMA tests with load 3 higher, and under (a, A) also the hippocampal slow theta to low gamma test (t = -3.21). The pre-SMA fast theta to high gamma test, absent from Table S1, has 7 to 21 channels here.
deviations: Artefact rejection without the visual inspection (O1). For band reading B the amplitude bandwidth is twice the band's centre frequency, by analogy with the comodulogram (not stated).

outcomes.notes: Refitted after round 2 with load 3 as the reference level, as Table S2 codes load (its load term is named "Load1"), so the PAC term is the slope in load 3 trials. With RT in s under artefact reading (a) (144 hippocampal channels, 16,103 correct clean trials), neither reading of O5 meets the criterion - under O5 (a) the hippocampal term is -53.0, t = -2.43, p = 0.015, but the amygdala term is also negative (p = 0.027); under O5 (b) the hippocampal term has p = 0.099. RT in s does not fit Table S2 - its intercept is 1.70 (O5 a) against the paper's 0.38. With RT z-scored over each session's correct trials the intercept is 0.28 and the Load1 term -0.32 (paper 0.38 and -0.48); under O5 (a) the hippocampal term is -49.39, t = -4.19, p = 2.8e-5 (paper -49.07, t = -4.01, p = 6e-5) but the amygdala term is -19.6, p = 0.015 (paper p = 0.48), and under O5 (b) the hippocampal term is negative (p = 0.029) with amygdala p = 0.20 and vmPFC p = 0.58, meeting the criterion. log10 RT splits the same way (O5 a, amygdala p = 0.036; O5 b, hippocampus p = 0.0045, amygdala 0.22, vmPFC 0.87). With RTs below 10 s (87 trials dropped), both readings meet the criterion (hippocampus p = 2.8e-7 and 0.00046; amygdala 0.097 and 0.097; vmPFC 0.99 and 0.61). Under artefact reading (b) every response scale and both O5 readings meet it (hippocampus p <= 0.031, amygdala >= 0.479, vmPFC >= 0.26). The slope in load 1 trials, which the first coding tested, has p = 0.25 and 0.64 with RT in s. On the scales that fit Table S2 the two readings of O5 disagree, which the criterion makes methods_underspecified; the change from not_reproduced was agreed in the third verification round. Table S2's PAC estimate (-49.07) points to O5 (a), under which the outcome would be not reproduced; this is asked of a reader.
deviations: The single-trial PAC is not described (O5); both readings of the claims file were run. Mixed model fitted with statsmodels MixedLM (REML), random intercepts for patient and for channel within patient, in place of MATLAB's fitglme. Load coded with load 3 as the reference (Supplementary Table S2, "Load 1 are tested against load 3 trials", with a term named "Load1").

Table S2 gives no unit or transform for RT. RT is fitted in s (the claims file's reading), as log10 RT and z-scored over each session's correct trials; the hippocampal trials under reading (a) have RTs up to 56.3 s (87 above 10 s), and a variant drops RTs above 10 s. The paper states no trimming.
Assumed artefact reading (a), as for edf2b-hippocampus-load-patients; under reading (b) every RT scale and both readings of O5 meet the criterion, which would give reproduced.

outcomes.notes: Under artefact reading (a), over 144 PAC channels, two load tests give p < 0.05 - high-gamma power is higher in load 3 (Hilbert t = 2.09, p = 0.035; Welch t = 2.69, p = 0.006) and the gamma peak frequency is higher in load 3 (93.0 against 86.8 Hz, t = 3.04, p = 0.003; as the coordinate of the single largest bin, p = 0.34). Theta power (p = 0.23, 0.16), rise-decay and peak-trough symmetry (all cycles p = 0.34 and 0.50; burst cycles, present in both loads in only 8 channels, p = 0.17 and 0.79), phase-phase locking (1 to 21, p = 0.90; each centre pair, p = 0.82), the theta peak frequency (p = 0.49; largest bin p = 0.080) and the preferred phase t-test (p = 0.71) do not differ. The V test of the phase differences against 0 gives p < 0.0001 (mean resultant length 0.94, circular mean -1.6 degrees), which shows differences concentrated at 0; the criterion's rule would count it as a test with p < 0.05, which is asked of a reader (questions/000673.yaml). No asymmetry differs from 0.5 (p >= 0.072). With two load tests significant the criterion gives not reproduced. Under artefact reading (b) (125 channels) no load test gives p < 0.05 (high-gamma power p = 0.13 and 0.058, gamma peak frequency p = 0.17).
deviations: Assumed artefact reading (a), as for edf2b-hippocampus-load-patients; the readings give different outcomes.

Theta waveform asymmetry from bycycle 1.2 with f_range 3-7 Hz and its default settings on each trial's -0.5 to 3 s epoch, cycles with their peak in 0 to 2.5 s, averaged per load over the trials of the PAC analysis (Methods, PAC - "We averaged estimates for peak-to-trough as well as rise-to-decay asymmetries across cycles during the maintenance period from the same trials used for our PAC analysis within each load"). Its burst detection fails under pandas 3 and is replaced by the same default thresholds applied to a writable copy. Whether only burst cycles count is not stated; both are shown. With the default thresholds 99.9% of trial windows have no burst cycle.

PAC peak frequency (Extended Data Fig. 3h legend - "recomputed PAC using a finer resolution for phase frequencies (i.e., a step size of 0.5 instead of 2 Hz) and determined the frequency bin for which PAC was maximal for the theta and the gamma band separately") from raw MI per load, phase centres 3 to 7 Hz in 0.5 Hz steps and amplitude centres 70 to 140 Hz; read as the maximum of the mean over the other axis, with the coordinates of the largest bin as a variant. Raw MI is used as no surrogates are described for this panel.
Phase-phase coupling under both readings of the criterion; for the second, n is the ratio of each amplitude centre to the phase centre, rounded to an integer.

outcomes.notes: Kappa of the theta-high-gamma amplitude distribution is lower in load 3 (a - 144 channels, 0.0360 against 0.0326, t = -4.54, p = 0.0001, 96 channels lower; b - 125 channels, t = -3.11, p = 0.0024). Paper t136 = -3.75, p = 0.0001.
deviations: Kappa from CircStat's circ_kappa formula on the 18 bin centres weighted by the normalized amplitude, as the criterion says.

outcomes.notes: Aligning the 500 ms windows on the gamma peak in each run of the preferred theta bin, 105 of 144 hippocampal PAC channels (72.92%) are nested under artefact reading (a), within tolerance of 110, and PAC is lower in load 3 in them (4.29 against 3.48, t = -3.61, p = 0.0002; paper t109 = -4.10, p = 0.0001); under (b) 94 of 125 (75.20%), p = 0.0051. Aligning on the maximum of gamma amplitude, as the Methods' words read, only 9 of 144 (6.25%) are nested and the load test fails (p = 0.77). The count depends on the alignment and not on the window - with local maxima counted within 35 to 85 ms the peak alignment gives 104 to 114 nested channels (30 within 25 ms), and the amplitude alignment 4 to 15 for every window.
deviations: Assumed that the windows are aligned on the peak of the gamma-filtered signal. The Methods say "the precise timepoint at which the concurrent instantaneous gamma amplitude (70-140 Hz) was maximal"; aligned on amplitude maxima, gamma cycles of random phase cancel in the average, so few local maxima remain (most channels have 0 or 1), which cannot give the paper's 80%. Aligned on gamma peaks, the average keeps the gamma cycle, as the method of Vaz et al. (ref. 69) needs.

outcomes.notes: Under artefact reading (a), raw theta-high-gamma MI is larger in load 1 (2.43e-4 against 2.17e-4, t = -4.03, p = 0.0002, 99 of 144 channels; paper t136 = -4.03, p = 0.0001). Under reading (b) p = 0.066 (125 channels).
deviations: Assumed artefact reading (a), as for edf2b-hippocampus-load-patients; the readings give different outcomes. On the one channel whose rejected trials the paper's code ships (artif_trials.mat with NWB_samplePAC_SU.m, sub-26 session 1, LFP channel 33), the paper removes 17 trials; reading (a) removes 4, all among them, and reading (b) removes 9, 5 of which the paper kept.

outcomes.notes: Over 586 hippocampal channels, the 2-150 Hz slope is -1.7260 +/- 0.4253 in load 1 and -1.7300 +/- 0.4314 in load 3 (paper -1.7526 and -1.7517, within tolerance), and the paired permutation test finds a difference (t = 2.66, p = 0.0073; artefact reading b, p = 0.0018). Over 30-150 Hz the slopes are -1.838 and -1.842 and the test does not find one (p = 0.12 and 0.28). The difference is 0.004, about 1% of the s.d. across channels.
deviations: Assumed the 2-150 Hz range. The frequency range and spectral estimate are not given; the two readings give different outcomes. The 2-150 Hz mean slope (-1.726) is closer to the paper's (-1.75) than the 30-150 Hz one (-1.84). Welch spectra (1 s Hann windows, 50% overlap) and the exclusion of 58-62 and 118-122 Hz are standard choices.

outcomes.notes: Not run in this attempt. Spike-field coherence (40 Morlet wavelets, 500 spike subsamples and 500 jittered surrogates per neuron-channel pair and condition, cluster tests with 10,000 permutations) was not written into a notebook, so no timing of it is shown and it is not blocked as too large. The data it needs (spikes, LFP, bundles inferred from location and coordinates) are in the dataset.

Under artefact reading (a), 166 hippocampal pairs of a category neuron and a significant PAC channel of its bundle (52 neurons, 15 patients; paper 151) and 450 amygdala pairs (paper 423). Refitted after round 2 with load 3 as the reference level, as Table S3 codes load, so the SC term is the slope in load 3 trials. The hippocampal SC term is positive with p < 0.05 under every reading - all correct trials, O5 (a) t = 6.34, p = 2.3e-10, O5 (b) 0.0045, t = 3.09, p = 0.0020 (paper 0.002, t = 2.40, p = 0.017); preferred trials, O5 (a) t = 3.09, p = 0.0020, O5 (b) 0.0028, t = 2.16, p = 0.031. The amygdala term has p >= 0.326 under every reading (paper p = 0.45). Under O5 (b) on all trials the other terms are close to Table S3 - intercept -0.057 (paper -0.044), Load1 0.078 (0.076), SC x Load1 -0.0049, p = 0.0002 (-0.004, p = 0.010). The slope in load 1 trials, which the first coding tested, is not positive (all trials O5 b, p = 0.77; preferred O5 b, -0.0045, p = 0.015), and neither is the paper's (0.002 - 0.004). Under artefact reading (b) (145 and 410 pairs) the hippocampal term is positive with p <= 0.014 under three readings and p = 0.056 under the fourth (preferred, O5 b); the amygdala term has p >= 0.32 (one of its fits did not converge). The change from not_reproduced was agreed in the third verification round.
deviations: Pairs as in the criterion; the claim's depends_on (fig3f-gamma-sfc-preferred) names the SFC pairs, which are the same category neuron and PAC channel pairs, so the claim was run without the SFC. Bundles are the electrodes of a session with the same location and coordinates.

Mixed model fitted with statsmodels MixedLM (REML), random intercepts for patient and for pair within patient, in place of fitglme, with load 3 as the reference level (Supplementary Table S3, "Load 1 are tested against load 3 trials", with a term named "Load1"). Artefact reading (a) assumed, as for edf2b-hippocampus-load-patients; under reading (b) one of the four readings has p = 0.056.

outcomes.notes: With FDR over all combinations of an area and load (O9 a), 8 of 269 hippocampal neurons (2.97%) and 5 of 422 amygdala neurons (1.18%) qualify, against 79 of 212 and 163 of 358; with FDR over each neuron's channels (b), 12 and 24. Every shuffled count is lower than the observed count (shuffle maxima 1 and 1 under a, 5 and 4 under b), p = 0.005 in both areas under both readings, so the shuffle test holds and the counts are far out of tolerance. Without FDR, 1.8% of neuron-channel-load combinations pass both tests at p < 0.01, against 0.1% in the shuffles. 269 and 422 MTL neurons have LFP in their bundle, against the paper's 212 and 358. Without any correction, 41 hippocampal and 66 amygdala neurons have a combination passing both tests at p < 0.01 (shuffles at most 13 and 14), still fewer than the paper's counts after FDR. The paper's plot_PAC_neuron.m fits the three GLMs to the 20 aggregated bin counts of one neuron-channel pair with fixed effects only, as sbcat.py does, so neither a per-trial layout nor a random effect explains the difference.
deviations: Selection as in plot_PAC_neuron.m (20 theta-gamma bins, three Poisson GLMs, likelihood-ratio tests), fitted by IRLS in Python in place of fitglme (deviances checked against statsmodels). Artefact rejection reading (a) without visual inspection. The FDR family is not stated (O9); both readings were run. Bundles are taken as the electrodes of a session with the same location and coordinates, as the files name no bundle.

outcomes.notes: Too few PAC neurons under the claim's own selection (8 hippocampal and 5 amygdala, against 79 and 163) for the overlap to describe the paper's populations. For the record, 4 of 8 and 2 of 5 are category neurons; the binomial test gives p = 0.16 and 0.57 and the hypergeometric test p = 0.13 and 0.64.

findings.statement: Spike times are not sorted in four units of two files. In sub-13 ses-1, units 6, 14 and 15 jump back by up to 1,319 to 1,339 s (units 6 and 15 once, unit 14 three times), as if two spike trains had been concatenated; in sub-22 ses-2, unit 10 steps back 24 times by up to 3.3 ms. The analysis sorts them, which keeps the result of the paper's code (it selects spikes with logical masks).

The files do not mark the LFP trials, channels or regions that the paper's artefact rejection removed, most of it by visual inspection (20.4 +/- 13.9 trials per wire, and whole wires or regions). The automated rules of the Methods remove 11.4% (on the epochs) or 25.9% (on whole trials) of trials, and the remaining channels change several results. The pre-SMA has 17 channels with significant theta-high-gamma PAC where the paper has 5, and they decide three claims of absence. 269 hippocampal and 422 amygdala neurons have LFP in their bundle, where the paper analysed 212 and 358 ("pre-processing steps removed broadband LFPs for some of the neurons"). The paper's code ships the rejected trials of one example channel (artif_trials.mat, sub-26 session 1, channel 33, 17 trials), which shows the information exists for the paper's own analysis.

The files do not identify the microwire bundles that the analyses pair neurons and LFPs within. Every wire is its own ElectrodeGroup, and the location names only area and hemisphere; some locations of a session hold up to 15 wires, and 26 of 285 location groups have more than one set of coordinates. Bundles were inferred from location and coordinates.

The maintenance period lasts 2.53 to 3.20 s in the trials table (probe onset minus maintenance onset), against 2.55 to 2.85 s in the Methods, and the blank between pictures in load 3 lasts 0.011 to 0.341 s, against 17 to 200 ms. RTs reach 74.2 s (69 trials above 10 s).

The paper cites version 0.240118.2135, which this attempt used. In the latest published version, 0.250122.0110, each of the 44 files has a new asset a few hundred kilobytes smaller; the attempt did not compare their contents.

Question for the authors - are the firing-rate tests of Fig. 3b-d and Fig. 4 computed on rates in Hz or on the percentage change from baseline shown in the panels? The two give different outcomes for Fig. 3b (preferred against non-preferred), Fig. 3c and Fig. 3d; this attempt assumed the percentage change.

Question for the authors - in the automated LFP artefact rejection, over what span are the channel's samples z-scored and tested (the -0.5 to 3 s maintenance epochs, or whole trials)? The two give different outcomes for Extended Data Fig. 2b and 3f; this attempt assumed the epochs, which agree with the paper's rejected trials on the one channel its code ships.

Question for the authors - for theta-gamma nesting (Extended Data Fig. 3e), are the 500 ms windows centred on the maximum of gamma amplitude or on a peak of the gamma-filtered signal? Centred on amplitude maxima, 6% of PAC channels are nested here; on gamma peaks, 73%. This attempt assumed gamma peaks.

Question for the authors - over what frequency range, and with what spectral estimate, was the log-log slope compared between loads (Methods, LFP preprocessing)? With Welch spectra, 2 to 150 Hz gives a small but significant difference (p = 0.0073) and 30 to 150 Hz none; this attempt assumed 2 to 150 Hz.

Question for the authors - how is single-trial theta-gamma PAC computed for the mixed-effects GLMs (Fig. 2f, 3h, 4c), and is RT transformed in the model of Table S2? Table S3's negative intercept (-0.044) rules out the raw MI as the response there, while Table S2's PAC estimate (-49.07) fits the raw MI as the predictor with RT z-scored within session (-49.39 here). Table S2 gives no unit for RT, and RT in s gives an intercept of 1.70 against its 0.38. With load 3 as the reference, the hippocampal relation to RT holds on z-scored or log RT, but the amygdala term is also significant under the raw MI (p = 0.015).

Question for the authors - which family is the FDR correction of the PAC neuron selection taken over, and what else differs from plot_PAC_neuron.m? Run as in that function on the dandiset, 8 of 269 hippocampal and 5 of 422 amygdala neurons qualify (12 and 24 with FDR over each neuron's channels), against 79 of 212 and 163 of 358.

The verifier queried the archive metadata and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. disagreements.reason: Under artefact (a), gamma power is higher in load 3 by both estimates (p = 0.035 and 0.006); theta power, phase-phase coupling and the preferred-phase t-test show no difference. Waveform asymmetry, peak frequency and the second phase-phase-coupling ratio were not run. A V test of the load differences against 0 tests concentration around 0, so a significant V test supports no phase shift; the claims file's reading (a), with its rule that no test gives p < 0.05, misreads the test (problem 5).

In Hz - preferred trials p = 0.022 (load 1 higher), non-preferred p = 0.20. In % - preferred p = 0.77. Under O6 (b), which % change with at least 1 incorrect trial supports by reproducing the paper's frontal n exactly (201, 180, 201), fig3c fails (problem 3).

The overlap does not exceed chance (p = 0.13 and 0.57), but the counts (4 and 2) are far out of tolerance and rest on n = 8 and 5. Every claim built on PAC neurons is run at n = 8 and 5 and cannot test the paper (problem 1).

Hippocampal SC term p = 0.85 and 0.18; amygdala p = 0.050 and 0.041. Only 8 and 5 pairs, so this is not an informative test. Every claim built on PAC neurons is run at n = 8 and 5 and cannot test the paper (problem 1).

Correct > incorrect holds (p = 0.02-0.03); maintenance against baseline fails (p = 0.51); n = 8 against 63. Every claim built on PAC neurons is run at n = 8 and 5 and cannot test the paper (problem 1).
Both baseline tests fail, and load 3 < load 1 is significant (p = 0.009); n = 8. Every claim built on PAC neurons is run at n = 8 and 5 and cannot test the paper (problem 1).
Baseline test p = 0.12 fails; the other three tests are null as claimed; n = 5. Every claim built on PAC neurons is run at n = 8 and 5 and cannot test the paper (problem 1).
fig3h appears nowhere - it is not in any notebook's table and not covered by the blocked line, yet every input it needs (category neurons x PAC channels) is already computed (problem 2).

entries.name: 000673-daume-2024
entries.title: Phase-amplitude coupling and working memory in human hippocampus (Daume et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Daume et al. (2024) on dandiset 000673, which holds 44 sessions of a Sternberg working memory task in 36 epilepsy patients, with 1,454 single neurons and 1,922 microwire LFP channels from the hippocampus, amygdala, pre-SMA, dACC and vmPFC. It tests the cohort, behaviour, category neurons and their maintenance activity, and the LFP theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, its load effect and its controls, single-trial PAC against reaction time and category neuron firing, and the selection and firing of PAC neurons. The spike-field coherence, noise correlation and decoding analyses were not run.
